title: The Vision of Linked Open Data and the Open Data Cloud
description: Linked Open Data (LOD) addresses the problem of data silos by making data publicly available and providing standard technology to easily link disparate datasets. The ultimate goal is to combine these linked data sources to build new applications and foster an interconnected data web.
summary:
The speaker introduces Linked Open Data (LOD) as a solution to the problem of data being trapped in silos, which makes querying and interlinking data difficult. Linked open data is defined as making data more publicly available and supplying standard technology to easily link different data sources.

The current landscape shows that many large datasets are now exposed by various governmental and commercial organizations globally. This ecosystem supports a vast cloud of open data, with a statistic noting approximately 16 billion public triples available, accessible via a standard query language called Sparkle.

The core vision of Linked Open Data is to use linked data standards to combine previously heterogeneous data sources. This allows users to easily find and combine this data to build new applications and innovative ways of viewing the combined information. The overall vision, echoing Tim Berners-Lee's philosophy, is to allow the data web to flourish.
